title: When the Tryouts Wakes
premise: Ivo Vasquez discovers that his grandmother's recipe box holds instructions for the Tryouts—the town of Marrow Bend's founding ritual, in which every generation feeds a piece of itself to the land to keep it alive. The town's beloved tradition is actually a slow devouring, and the elders who run it have been hiding the cost for decades. When Ivo's best friend is chosen as this year's offering, he must decide whether loyalty to the people who sheltered him matters more than the truth that could destroy them. In the end, Ivo rewrites the recipe—giving the land memory instead of flesh—and breaks the cycle at the price of his own invisibility, finally seen by everyone.
about_author: Mirabel Ishikawa grew up in a small farming town where everyone knew everyone's business and no one talked about the past. She writes stories about queer kids in close-knit places, finding magic in the recipes, rituals, and rumors families pass down.

chapters.title: Nine Hundred Neighbors
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Establishes Marrow Bend: graduation countdown, his carefully managed invisibility as the only out kid, and his warm but wary bond with grandma Rosa. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as safety, and the ache of wanting to leave.

chapters.title: The Recipe Box
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Cleaning out Rosa's pantry after her stroke, Ivo finds a card labeled not with ingredients but with names, dates, and a word he's never seen: 'offering.' Emotional beat: curiosity curdling into dread as the familiar kitchen turns strange.

chapters.title: Founding Day
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. The whole town gathers for the annual Tryouts festival—games, pies, a lottery nobody explains. Ivo watches Mayor Aldous Hale preside with unsettling reverence. Emotional beat: the uncanny feeling of seeing a beloved ritual from outside for the first time.

chapters.title: Denny's Name
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. His best friend Denny Okafor's name is drawn in the lottery; the crowd cheers while Denny laughs it off. Ivo alone notices the elders' faces go grim. Emotional beat: fear masked by celebration, and the first fracture in Ivo's trust.

chapters.title: What Grandma Knew
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Rosa, half-lucid, tells Ivo the recipe box was hers to keep 'until someone asked the right question.' She warns him: the land eats what the town feeds it. Emotional beat: grief braided with inheritance—a legacy he never wanted.

chapters.title: Loyalty Lessons
chapters.summary: Denny's POV. Denny embraces being chosen—it means honor, college money, his family's pride restored. He pulls Ivo closer, sensing Ivo's doubt. Emotional beat: the tenderness and danger of loving someone who believes the lie you've uncovered.

chapters.title: The Elders' Kitchen
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Following the recipe cards' dates, Ivo sneaks into the community hall basement and finds ledgers listing every offering since 1891—including Rosa's sister. Emotional beat: horror at how deep the cover-up runs, and guilt over his own silence.

chapters.title: Mayor Hale's Offer
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Hale privately reveals he knows Ivo found the box, then offers him a deal: stay quiet, and Denny's 'tryout' will be symbolic, painless, like all the others lately. Emotional beat: temptation—the seductive logic of complicity.

chapters.title: Symbolic
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Researching old newspapers, Ivo learns the offerings were once real deaths; only in living memory did they become theater—but the land has grown sick anyway, crops failing, wells souring. Emotional beat: dawning understanding that the lie is failing on its own.

chapters.title: Rosa's Confession
chapters.summary: Rosa's POV, lucid at last. She confesses she falsified her own tryout forty years ago, cheating the ritual—and the land remembers what it was owed. Emotional beat: a grandmother's shame becoming her grandson's burden.

chapters.title: Telling Denny
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Ivo shows Denny the ledgers; Denny refuses to believe, accusing Ivo of jealousy and of stealing his moment of belonging. Their friendship shatters. Emotional beat: the cruelty of truth arriving too early.

chapters.title: The Land Itself
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Out past the tree line, Ivo finds the field where offerings were made: soil black and hungry, whispering with voices of the taken, including a girl's voice that says Rosa's name. Emotional beat: awe and terror—the antagonist made landscape.

chapters.title: An Ally in the Archive
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Marisol, the librarian's daughter and Ivo's quiet crush, reveals her own family lost someone to the Tryouts and has been collecting evidence for years. Emotional beat: relief and first love—being seen without flinching.

chapters.title: Hale Tightens the Grip
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Hale, sensing exposure, moves the ceremony up and seals the records, painting Ivo as a troublemaker threatening the town's soul. Even Ivo's parents waver. Emotional beat: isolation deepening—truth-tellers punished as traitors.

chapters.title: What Loyalty Costs
chapters.summary: Denny's POV. Denny glimpses the black field himself during a midnight dare and feels the hunger under the soil. Shaken, he still can't abandon the identity the Tryouts gave him. Emotional beat: tragic self-deception, loyalty weaponized against him.

chapters.title: Rewriting the Recipe
chapters.summary: Ivo, Marisol, and Rosa work from Rosa's original notes: the ritual's first version asked the land for partnership, not sacrifice—memory given freely instead of lives taken. But it requires an offering of true name and story. Emotional beat: hope forged from inherited knowledge.

chapters.title: The Night Before
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. The town prepares the ceremony; Denny asks Ivo to stand beside him tomorrow, a gesture of reconciliation. Ivo, planning to hijack the rite, must lie to his best friend one last time. Emotional beat: bittersweet intimacy shadowed by deception.

chapters.title: Tryouts
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. At the ceremony, Hale begins the rite; the field's hunger surges visibly, crops dying at the edges of the crowd. Ivo steps into the circle before Denny can. Emotional beat: sacrifice as the ultimate act of love for a flawed home.

chapters.title: The Offering of Names
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV, climax. Instead of flesh, Ivo speaks every name in the ledgers aloud—giving the land its stolen memories back. The ground convulses; Hale tries to stop him and is pulled toward the soil he fed for years. Emotional beat: cathartic confrontation, truth spoken at maximum cost.

chapters.title: Seen
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. The bargain takes its price: Ivo's careful invisibility burns away—he becomes unforgettable, known to all nine hundred neighbors, his queerness and his defiance public forever. Denny publicly chooses him over the elders. Emotional beat: terror and liberation entwined.

chapters.title: After the Harvest
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. The town reels: Hale gone, the ledgers read aloud at a town meeting, some families furious, others grieving and grateful. The fields green again. Rosa, fading, tells Ivo she's proud. Emotional beat: messy communal reckoning rather than easy forgiveness.

chapters.title: Graduation Day
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Ivo walks at graduation no longer counting days, hand in hand with Marisol, Denny cheering too loud in the stands. He leaves the rewritten recipe box with the town—not as a secret, but as a covenant. Emotional beat: belonging earned through truth; an ending that opens outward.
